name: Citi
summary: Citi's student hiring, as its careers site describes it, usually runs from a skills evaluation (a coding assessment for technology programmes) to a one-on-one first interview on your background and goals, then a final stage of several interviews, an assessment or a case study. Interviews often reflect Citi's Leadership Principles: we take ownership, we deliver with pride and we succeed together.
rounds: Skills evaluation: a coding assessment for technology programmes, or a skills survey for some others
First interview: one-on-one, on your background and how your goals fit Citi
Final stage: several interviews, an assessment or a case study, varying by programme and location
looks_for: Care with risk, controls and accuracy
Understanding clients' needs, including clients that work across countries
Clear problem solving in technical or case questions

questions.text: Tell me about yourself and why you applied to this programme.
covers: Your background in a few lines, focused on what's relevant
One achievement that shows the skills the programme needs
How the programme fits what you want to do next

questions.text: Tell me about a time you took ownership of a problem nobody else had picked up.
covers: What the problem was and why it had been left
What you did, step by step, and who you brought in
The result and how you made sure it stayed fixed

questions.text: Tell me about a piece of work you were proud of because of how carefully it was done.
covers: What the work was and why care mattered
The checks and standards you set yourself
How it was received and what it led to

questions.text: Describe a time you learnt something important from someone with a very different view.
covers: How their view differed from yours
What you did to understand it rather than argue
How it changed the result or your thinking

questions.text: Tell me about a time you spotted a risk early. What did you do?
covers: The risk and how you noticed it
Who you told and what you proposed
What was avoided, and what you learnt

questions.text: What does a bank's treasury and trade services business do for a multinational company?
covers: Managing cash across countries: collecting, paying and moving money
Trade finance, such as letters of credit, that helps companies buy and sell abroad
Why companies value it: visibility of cash, lower risk, less manual work

questions.text: Explain foreign exchange risk to a company that sells abroad, and one way it can reduce it.
covers: Revenue in another currency can be worth less when converted back
Hedging with forward contracts or options, or matching costs to the same currency
The trade-off: certainty against cost and giving up gains

questions.text: Why do banks put so many controls on payments, and what could go wrong without them?
covers: Controls such as approvals, limits, sanctions screening and reconciliations
Risks without them: fraud, errors, money laundering, regulatory penalties
Balancing strong controls with fast service for clients

questions.text: How would you design a service that sends payments across countries and makes sure none is sent twice?
covers: A unique ID for each payment so a retry can't create a second one
Recording each payment's state and confirming with the receiving side
Handling failures, timeouts and audits, and reconciling at the end of each day

questions.text: Explain the difference between a REST API and a message queue, and when you'd use each.
covers: REST: a caller asks and waits for an answer; a queue: messages are left for others to process
REST for lookups and immediate actions; queues for spikes, retries and decoupled systems
An example from a project you've worked on

questions.text: A key report for regulators is late every month. How would you find out why and fix it?
covers: Mapping the steps, data sources and owners behind the report
Finding where time goes: late data, manual fixes, approvals
A fix with clear owners, and a check that the report is right as well as on time

questions.text: Why Citi, and why this programme?
covers: What the programme does and the clients it serves
Why that work fits your skills and interests
Something specific about Citi you learnt from its people or events

questions.text: Where do you want to be in five years, and how would this role help you get there?
covers: A realistic goal linked to the programme
The skills and experience you expect to build
Commitment to doing this role well first

tips: Citi says its first interview goes into your background and how your aspirations align with Citi's; have a short, clear story linking the two.
Prepare an example for each Leadership Principle: taking ownership, delivering with pride and succeeding together.
Citi serves many clients that work across countries; be ready to discuss cross-border payments, trade and currency basics.
For technology programmes, practise coding problems under time limits and explain your code's complexity and how you'd test it.
If the final stage includes a case study, set out your structure, show the numbers you used, and end with a recommendation.
